description: Generic sk-language searches combining vestník/EKS terms with 'bankomat' and 'platobný terminál' returned portal homepages and methodology pages, not concrete award notices. Notice-level hits appear to require in-portal search (CPV/full-text) rather than general web search indexing.

result.result_summary: No specific SK ATM/payment-terminal award notice was retrieved via web search in this pass.

why_it_matters: Collection design must assume in-portal querying (ÚVO search, EKS search, CRZ full-text) rather than relying on search-engine discovery; notice bodies are largely invisible to external crawlers.

description: Could not confirm dedicated buyer-profile URLs for Štátna pokladnica and DataCentrum (now largely absorbed into MIRRI/other bodies) in this pass; only the generic ÚVO profile-search mechanism and MIRRI's profile page were confirmed.

result.result_summary: Buyer-specific procurement profile URLs for Štátna pokladnica and DataCentrum not identified.

why_it_matters: These are named target buyers in the cell; their profile IDs must be resolved directly in the ÚVO profile register before monitoring can start.

description: The JOSEPHINE SK entry URL was inferred from the platform's known structure and from monitors naming it as a data source; it was not opened in this pass.

result.result_summary: JOSEPHINE listed with moderate confidence and no example URLs.

why_it_matters: Prevents recording an unconfirmed URL as verified; the correct entry point should be resolved by following a JOSEPHINE link contained in an ÚVO notice.

description: Reporting indicates a large share of SK public contracts (~75% in 2025 per one secondary source) are not awarded via open calls, and only above-EU-threshold contracts reach TED.

result.result_summary: TED-only or open-call-only collection would systematically miss most SK activity.

why_it_matters: Direct-award and below-threshold channels (EKS, CRZ, buyer portals) must be first-class collection targets, not fallbacks.

description: Slovak disclosure law exempts contracts concluded within Štátna pokladnica's remit that relate to financial and payment services, as well as contracts securing the provision of payment services, from mandatory publication.

result.result_summary: Searching in Slovak for Štátna pokladnica contract disclosure surfaced the exemption rather than a browsable treasury contract stream; the treasury's payment-gateway relationships appear only as product terms documents on pokladnica.sk, not as signed supplier contracts.

why_it_matters: Absence of a payments contract in CRZ cannot be read as absence of a relationship. Any vendor-share or win/loss inference built on CRZ must carry this exemption caveat, especially for the treasury and bank-side payment services that are the core of this sector.

description: No official, documented REST API for CRZ was found; the sanctioned machine route is XML change-batch dumps via the national open-data catalogue, and the community record shows the practical APIs are third-party (uvostat, paid, ~6 req/min).

result.result_summary: The Slovensko.Digital platform hosts a standing 'Centrálny register zmlúv API' request thread and a mirrors thread, both pointing to third-party solutions rather than an official endpoint.

why_it_matters: Collection design must budget for bulk XML ingestion plus targeted HTML fetching, or for a paid third-party API — not for a free official API. Rate limits shape how fast a backfill can run.

description: Known CRZ bulk distributions (SQL dump, CSV of documents, torrent) carry metadata and document URLs but not the PDF files themselves; the full document archive was described as roughly 1TB.

result.result_summary: Explicitly stated in the Slovensko.Digital mirror thread ('neobsahuje' the documents).

why_it_matters: Unit prices, SLAs and subcontractor lists live inside the PDFs, not the metadata. A two-stage pipeline is required: metadata bulk load, then selective PDF fetch on keyword/IČO matches, with OCR budget for scanned annexes.

description: The NBS contracts page returned its column headers but an empty data table to a plain HTML fetch on the run date.

result.result_summary: Fields Názov zmluvy / Zmluvný partner / IČO / Predmet zmluvy / Dátum uzavretia / Dátum zverejnenia were present; no rows rendered.

why_it_matters: This is a hypothesis about client-side rendering, not evidence the register is empty. Collection needs a JS-capable fetcher or the underlying JSON endpoint; do not record NBS as a dead source.

description: The otvorenezmluvy.sk application itself never surfaced in results; only the Transparency International Slovensko announcement page describing it was reachable.

result.result_summary: Slovak-language query naming the portal returned the TIS article and unrelated registers.

why_it_matters: The NGO overlay may be dormant. Its eleven-criterion risk scoring is worth replicating in-house regardless, but it should not be listed as an active feed until liveness is verified by the deterministic pass.

description: The data.gov.sk CRZ dataset URL 302-redirected to the root of the new portal data.slovensko.sk, so the dataset's current landing page and distribution URLs were not confirmed in this pass.

result.result_summary: HTTP 302 from https://data.gov.sk/es/dataset/crz to https://data.slovensko.sk/.

why_it_matters: A migration is under way; the dataset almost certainly still exists under a new path. Recorded as moved/unverified rather than dead, and the exact distribution URLs must be re-resolved before building the ingestion job.

description: The Slovak term 'bankomat' in contract registers is dominated by real-estate leases of the few square metres an ATM stands on, signed by banks with municipalities.

result.result_summary: The first CRZ hits for 'bankomat' were an ATM-space lease from Slovenská sporiteľňa with Mesto Svätý Jur and a non-residential lease with ČSOB from Obec Rozhanovce — placement, not servicing.

why_it_matters: Naive keyword collection will fill the corpus with siting leases and miss the servicing/CIT/hardware contracts. Query design must combine 'bankomat' with servis/údržba/prevádzka/dopĺňanie hotovosti, or filter by supplier IČO of known vendors instead. Note the leases are still useful for ATM-footprint mapping — just a different signal.

description: Several high-value local terms in this cell's glossary were not yet run as searches in this pass: 'spracovanie hotovosti', 'prevoz cenín', 'peňažné prostriedky', 'dopĺňanie bankomatov', 'akceptácia platobných kariet', 'core banking systém', 'bankový informačný systém', 'samoobslužná zóna', 'recyklačný bankomat', 'platobná brána'.

result.result_summary: Coverage so far concentrated on register discovery rather than exhaustive term sweeps.

why_it_matters: Source discovery is adequate, but term coverage inside those sources is not. Without these terms the cash-logistics and core-banking sub-topics are under-sampled relative to POS/ATM.

description: Apart from the CRZ English UI shell, no English-language source specific to Slovak public contract registers for banking/payments was found; English queries returned generic or non-Slovak results.

result.result_summary: The English seed query surfaced the CRZ English portal and Wikipedia entries on NBS, nothing substantive.

why_it_matters: Confirms that all substantive collection in this cell must be Slovak-language, and that contract subject matching, glossary work and any classifier must operate in Slovak including diacritic-insensitive variants.

description: No statutory SK register exposes a 'banking/payments technology vendor' category. RÚZ, ORSR and RPVS are entity-keyed only; sector slicing must be reconstructed externally via SK NACE codes (e.g. 62.01/62.09/63.11/26.20/95.11) or a manually curated IČO watchlist.

result.result_summary: Searched sk-language terms for supplier-of-banking-systems filings; register search UIs offer name/IČO/seat filters, not activity+revenue screening. Only commercial aggregators (FinStat databáza firiem, sortable by sales and region) provide that screening.

why_it_matters: The vendor universe cannot be discovered from the registers themselves; the registers only verify and size entities already identified from other cells. Pipeline must therefore start from a name list.

description: Slovakia has no free, bulk, machine-readable beneficial-ownership dataset covering all companies. RPVS covers only public-sector partners, and the AML register of beneficial owners (register konečných užívateľov výhod maintained within the commercial register under AML law) is not publicly browsable in the same way.

result.result_summary: Searches on konečný užívateľ výhod returned RPVS and the historic ÚVO register; no evidence found of an open, all-company UBO download.

why_it_matters: UBO coverage for private-sector-only vendors will be partial; ownership chains for vendors with no public-sector contracts must be inferred from ORSR shareholder entries and Foaf.sk graphs, with lower confidence.

description: This cell yielded essentially nothing for the 'case studies' topic. Statutory registers publish financials and ownership, not deployment references.

result.result_summary: Closest proxies found: RPVS verifikačné dokumenty (which sometimes narrate contracts and group structure) and RÚZ poznámky/výročné správy (which may name major customers or segments) — both indirect and inconsistent.

why_it_matters: Case-study evidence must come from other cells (vendor sites, procurement records, press); register cells should not be expected to deliver it.

description: The exact current RPO public endpoint/API base was not confirmed in-session; two different Statistical Office paths appeared (rpo.statistics.sk/rpo and a portal wcm path).

result.result_summary: Search results referenced slovensko.sk and https://rpo.statistics.sk/rpo as service entry points; no fetch was performed to confirm which is canonical today.

why_it_matters: A pipeline built on the wrong RPO base URL would silently fail; verify before integration. Recorded as unverified, not dead.

description: AmCham Slovakia does not appear to run a dedicated 'Financial Services Committee'. The standing committees found were Civil Code Task Force, Business-Academic Cooperation, Digital, Employment and Social Affairs, Energy, Health Care, Public Procurement Task Force, Rule of Law Initiative and Tax.

result.result_summary: The seed-query assumption of an AmCham financial-services committee is not supported; the Digital Committee and Tax Committee are the nearest relevant bodies.

why_it_matters: Collection should target the Digital Committee outputs rather than waiting for a financial-services committee that may not exist; avoids a permanent empty watchlist entry.

description: Slovenská FinTech asociácia (slovakfintech.sk) and Slovensko-nemecká obchodná a priemyselná komora do not expose a complete public member list in search-visible form; only officers, aggregate counts or partial lists were found.

result.result_summary: Membership must be reconstructed indirectly via the state register of interest associations (rez.vs.minv.sk), FinStat/Transparex, or event sponsor pages.

why_it_matters: Directory-diffing pipelines will produce false 'no members' results for these bodies unless the indirect route is configured.

description: The acronym 'SIBA' as a Slovak blockchain/investment association did not resolve to any real organisation in SK searches; 'SAPI' resolves to the sustainable-energy association, not fintech.

result.result_summary: Searching these acronyms returns unrelated bodies; the real blockchain actors are Blockchain Slovakia and Slovenská kryptomenová asociácia.

why_it_matters: Flags SIBA and SAPI as noisy/false-friend acronyms that must be excluded from SK query templates to avoid polluting the actor map.

description: No SK association was found to publish an explicit list of technology vendors serving banks, or sponsor lists in a machine-readable form. Sponsor identification will depend on event pages and PDF programmes.

result.result_summary: Sponsor-based vendor discovery is possible but manual/semi-structured across SBA, ITAS, AmCham, Britcham and AHK event pages.

why_it_matters: Sets realistic expectations for the collection routine: sponsor logos are images and PDFs, needing OCR rather than HTML parsing.

description: SBCB (SRBI) and NBCB (NRKI) credit-register content is protected by banking secrecy and GDPR; only corporate/member pages are collectible.

result.result_summary: Public 'o nás' and member pages are fair game; register data is not.

why_it_matters: Prevents a compliance incident if a downstream collector treats these domains as generally scrapable.

description: No dedicated, SK-specific banking-technology trade fair or exhibition with a published exhibitor floor plan was found. Unlike larger CEE markets, Slovakia appears to have no equivalent of a standalone payments/banking-tech expo; vendor presence is expressed through sponsor tiers at general IT (ITAPA), fintech (Finweek) or association (ZBK) events instead.

result.result_summary: Searched sk and en for veľtrh/výstava/expo + banky/platby; only general career and health expos and the ITAPA EXPO zone surfaced.

why_it_matters: Collection design must not assume an exhibitor-list format; the roster signal has to be reconstructed from partner logo walls and agendas across several events.

description: The term 'Zlatý dukát' as a Slovak banking award produced no results; it appears not to be an SK award name (possible confusion with Czech usage or with the coin product).

result.result_summary: Query returned only Zlatá minca, TREND Banka roka and Mastercard Awards; no 'Zlatý dukát' SK award.

why_it_matters: Prevents a fabricated award entity entering the actor map; confirms Zlatá minca is the dominant SK product-award brand.

description: Could not confirm a standing dedicated banking section ('banková sekcia') within ITAPA. Search surfaced ITAPA Health & Care and general digitalisation programmes; banking relevance at ITAPA appears indirect (state digital identity, eID, eDOKLADY) rather than a named financial track.

result.result_summary: ITAPA programme pages examined via search results only; no banking track identified.

why_it_matters: ITAPA should be treated as an indirect/vendor-mapping source for banking rather than a direct banking-agenda source; downgrade expectations for banking-specific agenda mining there.

description: Individual per-edition ITAPA partner/exhibitor listing pages were not retrieved in this pass — only the hub pages (/virtualna-vystava-itapa-partnerov/, /archiv-podujati/) were identified. The specific logo-wall URLs per year remain unresolved and unverified.

result.result_summary: Hub URLs identified; per-year partner list URLs not enumerated.

why_it_matters: The collection pass must crawl rather than fetch fixed URLs; a naive single-URL fetch will miss the multi-year sponsor history that gives this cell its timing value.

description: The organiser and canonical domain of the 'IT vo finančníctve' conference (Bratislava, Austria Trend hotel) was not resolved; it is currently reachable only through the konferencie.sk/education.sk aggregator listing and a pravnenoviny.sk write-up.

result.result_summary: Aggregator listing found; organiser homepage not identified.

why_it_matters: This is potentially the single most on-target SK banking-IT agenda; failing to resolve its organiser leaves the highest-relevance vendor roster unharvested.

description: Qubit Conference Slovakia advertises a deliberately 'vendor-free' programme and no sponsor/partner roster was located in this pass, only speaker pages.

result.result_summary: Speaker page found; partner/sponsor page not located.

why_it_matters: For this event the exploitable signal is speaker affiliation, not sponsorship — collection method must differ from Finweek/ITAPA.

description: Local-language searches for a named Slovak core-banking migration project with an identified supplier (queries combining 'banka', 'migracia core bankoveho systemu', 'dodavatel', 'tender') returned no article-level hits from Trend, HN, Zive.sk or ITnews.sk.

result.result_summary: Only one concrete migration event surfaced (CSOB migrating former OTP Banka clients to new systems, via Banky.sk). No SK trade-press article naming a core-banking vendor selection was retrieved through general web search.

why_it_matters: Core-banking vendor selections in SK appear to be reported thinly or behind paywalls; discovery will require on-site archive search per outlet plus vendor press-clipping archives rather than general search engines.

description: Site-level searches did not surface any article-level content from itnews.sk despite it being named in the cell brief.

result.result_summary: itnews.sk produced no article hits in either SK or EN queries; only the cell brief attests to it.

why_it_matters: The outlet may have low search-engine indexing, be behind a portal structure, or be dormant. Its URL is recorded at reduced confidence and must be checked by the deterministic liveness pass rather than assumed live.

description: Zive.sk appears to have been folded into the Aktuality publishing group (zive.aktuality.sk); no direct zive.sk article URLs were returned.

result.result_summary: No zive.sk article-level result in either SK query; the working canonical host is uncertain between zive.sk and zive.aktuality.sk.

why_it_matters: Collectors keyed on the wrong host will silently return nothing. Both hosts should be probed and the canonical one pinned before scheduling a crawler.

description: Searching 'forbes.sk banky fintech' returned predominantly Forbes Czech (forbes.cz) results; SK/CZ brand bleed is a systematic risk for Trend, Forbes and HN which all have Czech sister titles.

result.result_summary: Forbes Slovensko was confirmed only via a separate query that returned forbes.sk directly.

why_it_matters: Any collection pipeline must hard-filter on the .sk host and on Slovak-language content, or CZ coverage will contaminate the SK market picture.

description: No dedicated Slovakia country tag/index page was located on The Paypers, unlike FinTech Futures which has one.

result.result_summary: The Paypers returned only generic global report pages for the Slovakia query.

why_it_matters: The Paypers must be collected via on-site keyword search on bank/PSP names rather than a country feed, which is more brittle and needs bespoke handling.

description: Live full-text query on Profesia.sk for 'Temenos' (https://www.profesia.sk/praca/?search_anywhere=Temenos) returned zero offers ('Lutujeme, ale nenasli sme ponuky vyhovujuce Vasim kriteriam'). The same query for 'Flexcube' also returned zero offers.

result.result_summary: 0 hits for Temenos; 0 hits for Flexcube on the largest SK job portal at time of scouting.

why_it_matters: Vendor brand names are NOT a reliable retrieval key in the Slovak market at any given moment - the installed base is small and ads are sparse. The collector must be built as a standing longitudinal alert (Profesia offers a saved-search email agent at /agent/) rather than a one-shot query, and must lean on Slovak functional phrases ('platobne systemy', 'kartove systemy', 'centralny bankovy system') which do return hits.

description: General web search engines returned essentially no SK-located job postings for the platform terms Base24, Postilion, ISO 8583, Vynamic, Way4, Mambu or Auriga; results were dominated by Wikipedia, US/Gulf job boards and vendor marketing pages.

result.result_summary: Web-search-mediated discovery of SK platform-specific job ads failed; only direct portal endpoint queries produced named SK employers.

why_it_matters: Confirms the collection design must query the SK portals' own search endpoints directly. Budgeting generic web search for this cell would produce a false negative on SK platform presence.

description: No Slovakia-specific careers hub was found for Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Voyix, Worldline or Global Payments; searches surfaced only global career pages and the Diebold Nixdorf Pilsen (CZ) global center.

result.result_summary: SK-country career endpoints for the major ATM/payments vendors were not located in this pass.

why_it_matters: ATM and acquiring vendor capacity serving Slovakia appears to be staffed regionally (CZ/PL/HU hubs) rather than locally. Vendor-capacity signals for SK must therefore be read from neighbouring-country hubs, which weakens country attribution and must be caveated in any conclusion.

description: LinkedIn job search and people/title search for Slovakia could not be exercised without authentication; only public company pages appeared in search results.

result.result_summary: LinkedIn title mining is not accessible to an unauthenticated automated collector, and its ToS prohibits scraping.

why_it_matters: The single richest title-mining source in this cell is legally and technically off-limits to automated collection. Plan for a licensed product or a documented manual analyst workflow; do not build a scraper.

description: No open-data API or bulk export was confirmed for the statutory vacancy register at sluzbyzamestnanosti.gov.sk; the search UI was documented but the backend interface was not established in this pass.

result.result_summary: Portal exists and is legally mandated, but machine access route is unknown - a hypothesis, not a dead end.

why_it_matters: If a structured feed exists it would be the highest-quality, lowest-risk collection route in the whole cell. Worth one dedicated technical probe (network inspection of the search UI, robots.txt, data.gov.sk catalogue) before falling back to HTML scraping.

description: Slovak IT integrators plausibly staffing bank projects (Soitron, NESS KDC, DXC Slovakia, Asseco Central Europe SK, Accenture SK, IBM Slovensko, Monet+, Gemalto/Thales SK) were named in the search but their individual career endpoints were not located or confirmed in this pass.

result.result_summary: Integrator layer of the actor map is identified conceptually but not yet resolved to URLs.

why_it_matters: Integrators, not banks, write the most explicit platform requirements ('skusenost s T24', 'znalost ISO 8583'). Leaving this layer unresolved is the largest remaining gap in the cell.

description: No public source identified naming the technology supplier(s) of self-checkout systems for Lidl SK, Tesco SR, Kaufland SK or Billa SK.

result.result_summary: Retailer press releases and Forbes.sk report deployment counts and strategy but never the vendor (NCR/Toshiba/Diebold/ITAB etc.); private retailers are outside the ÚVO tender regime, so no procurement trail exists.

why_it_matters: Vendor identity for the retail self-checkout estate is a core A6 question; it will require indirect proxies (installer job ads, integrator references, trade-fair material) rather than direct disclosure.

description: No Slovak Brink's entity or sk-language Brink's site surfaced.

result.result_summary: Searches in sk returned only Brink's Cash Solutions (CZ) and G4S/Securitas SK entities; Brink's SK presence is unconfirmed.

why_it_matters: The seed query assumed a SK Brink's; the actual SK CIT duopoly appears to be Loomis SK plus G4S/Securitas-lineage entities, which changes the competitor map.

description: No petrol-network (Slovnaft, OMV, Shell SK) source found for cashback or payment-acceptance infrastructure.

result.result_summary: The cashback query returned only COOP Jednota and general retail coverage; no fuel-retail cash-access or terminal-estate documentation surfaced.

why_it_matters: Petrol networks are an explicitly listed part of this cell and remain uncovered, leaving a buyer segment blank.

description: No tender document found for Bratislava DPB's open-loop contactless ticketing ('Kartuj' / 'Tapni sa').

result.result_summary: Operator news and imhd.sk describe the service and accepted schemes but not the acquirer, PSP or validator supplier; no ÚVO notice was retrieved in this pass.

why_it_matters: Bratislava is the flagship SK transit-payments reference; without the supplier chain the case study cannot be attributed.

description: No authoritative figure for the number of Euronet ATMs in Slovakia.

result.result_summary: Euronet SK's own pages give group-level scale (50,000+ ATMs worldwide) but no SK network size; NBS/SBA statistics do not appear to split bank vs independent deployer estates in the results seen.

why_it_matters: IAD share of the SK ATM estate is a headline metric for the non-bank buyer layer and currently has no verified source.

description: General web search could not surface a specific SK contract award notice under CPV 30123400 (ATM/banking machinery) or related banking CPVs; search engines index TED notices poorly and inconsistently.

result.result_summary: Only generic TED how-to guides and unrelated non-SK notices returned. Confirms that CPV-level SK banking procurement must be queried inside TED itself or via its API, not via general search.

why_it_matters: Sets the collection design: TED Search API with explicit country+CPV facets is required; keyword web search is not a viable discovery channel for this cell.

description: No public, per-transaction beneficiary list was found for EIF InvestEU/EFSI guarantees to Slovak intermediaries (SZRB, ČSOB, Komerční banka).

result.result_summary: EIF publishes intermediary-level deals (volumes, expected number of SMEs) but not final-beneficiary registers for SK.

why_it_matters: Limits the granularity of the funding trail: we can map which banks run EU-backed products, but not which end clients, so downstream vendor inference must rely on procurement rather than beneficiary data.

description: A WebFetch of https://ted.europa.eu/en/simap/faq returned HTTP 404.

result.result_summary: Treated as a moved/renamed page hypothesis, not as evidence TED's SIMAP area is dead — the developer/reuser pages under the same host were found via search and remain the correct entry point.

why_it_matters: Documents that one bad fetch is not a liveness verdict and that the reusers' corner URL should be used instead.

description: EBRD project procurement notices largely live behind ECEPP and corporate procurement behind SMART by GEP, both of which encourage or require supplier registration.

result.result_summary: Public notice listings appear to exist on ebrd.com, but full notice detail and award history may need an account.

why_it_matters: IFI supplier trails for SK financial institutions may be only partially collectible without registration; plan a manual/periodic review rather than automated ingestion.

description: No Slovak-language terminology was available for the IFI layer (EIB/EBRD/EIF procurement), because those institutions publish about Slovakia almost exclusively in English.

result.result_summary: SK-language searching was applied successfully to ÚVO, plán obnovy, ITMS and eurofondy, but IFI procurement had no meaningful SK vocabulary beyond institution names (Európska investičná banka, Slovenská záručná a rozvojová banka).

why_it_matters: Local-language coverage for this cell is inherently asymmetric: national/EU-funds layer is SK-rich, IFI layer is EN-only. Collection queries should reflect that split.

description: No publicly accessible, entity-level version of the DORA 'register of information' on ICT third-party contractual arrangements was found for Slovakia. NBS guidance confirms supervised firms must maintain and submit it from 17.1.2025, but the submitted data is supervisory and not published.

result.result_summary: Only guidance, templates and incident-reporting pages are public; no named vendor-to-institution mapping is downloadable.

why_it_matters: This would have been the single richest regulator-side dataset for A6 vendor mapping in SK banking; its confidentiality means vendor relationships must be reconstructed from tenders, press releases and vendor case studies instead.

description: No public participant list for the SIPS and TARGET2-SK payment systems was located on the current NBS site during this pass; only access-condition documents and news announcements were found.

result.result_summary: Access rules for non-bank PSPs (effective 6.10.2025) are published, but the roster of actual participants was not found at a stable URL.

why_it_matters: The participant roster would be the cleanest evidence of which institutions clear domestically versus via foreign infrastructure, and of new non-bank entrants.

description: No standalone recurring NBS 'payment systems oversight report' (an annual SIPS/TARGET2-SK oversight assessment as a separate publication) was identified; oversight outcomes appear folded into the NBS annual report and the financial-market supervision activity report.

result.result_summary: Searches in both sk and en returned framework and policy pages plus annual-report PDFs, not a dedicated oversight report series.

why_it_matters: Collection must target chapters inside larger annual reports rather than a clean report series, which raises parsing cost.

description: NBS publishes many primary documents behind opaque GUID CDN paths of the form https://nbs.sk/dokument/<uuid>/stiahnut?force=true, with no visible stable slug.

result.result_summary: PDF URLs discovered via search are not predictable or enumerable and are likely to change between site revisions.

why_it_matters: Any collector must resolve PDFs from their parent HTML section pages each run rather than hardcoding document URLs, or links will silently rot.

description: Liveness of the legacy www.nbs.sk/sk/platobne-systemy tree and of the /_img/documents/ PDF paths (e.g. politika_oversightu_nbs.pdf) was not confirmed in this pass.

result.result_summary: These URLs appear in search indexes but were not fetched; they may redirect to the redesigned site.

why_it_matters: Recorded as unverified hypotheses rather than dead links, per the run's verification protocol.

description: UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia, a.s., pobočka zahraničnej banky (IČO 47251336) has no Slovak-language investor-relations or annual-report page of its own; Slovak searches returned only register aggregators (registeruz, FinStat, D&B) and Wikipedia, not a bank-hosted výročná správa.

result.result_summary: Branch-level SK disclosure appears to route entirely through the Czech parent's výroční zpráva plus the Slovak RÚZ filing. No SK IR page located in this pass.

why_it_matters: UniCredit's Slovak technology decisions are made and disclosed in Prague/Milan, so any vendor-mention mining must target Czech- and Italian-language parent documents rather than SK sources — a language dimension outside this run's sk/en scope.

description: No standalone ČSOB Slovensko Pillar 3 / 'zverejňovanie informácií podľa Opatrenia NBS 16/2014' document was located in this pass — only the combined bilingual výročná správa PDFs from the /documents/11005/98584/ library.

result.result_summary: Search returned annual reports for 2016, 2018, 2020 and 2025 but no separate Pillar 3 file; the disclosures may be embedded in the annual report or on an unindexed sub-page.

why_it_matters: Pillar 3 operational-risk sections are where outsourcing dependencies surface most explicitly; if ČSOB embeds rather than separates them, the collector must parse whole annual reports instead of a small targeted document.

description: The only NBS 'Pilier III – výkazníctvo a zverejňovanie' page surfaced sits under the insurance (poisťovníctvo) supervision branch, not banking. The banking-sector disclosure-framework page on nbs.sk was not located in this pass.

result.result_summary: Slovak regulatory-term searches repeatedly returned the insurance Pillar III page as the top nbs.sk hit for both VÚB and Prima banka queries.

why_it_matters: Without the banking-sector NBS page the collection calendar for bank disclosure documents (cadence, mandatory templates, outsourcing-notification duties) rests on inference from bank documents rather than on the supervisor's own statement.

description: Named technology vendors were NOT found inside the Slovak banks' own annual reports in this pass. The two concrete vendor attributions obtained (Temenos payment hub at Tatra banka; PosAm end-user-services outsourcing at Tatra banka) both came from vendor-side marketing, not from bank disclosure.

result.result_summary: Bank annual reports surfaced digitalisation narratives and investment figures, but the search-result excerpts contained no supplier names.

why_it_matters: Confirms the cell rationale only partially: SK bank disclosures reliably reveal that transformation is happening and how much it costs, but who supplies it is more often revealed by vendor case studies and integrator reference pages. Collection design should pair both channels rather than relying on disclosures alone.

description: No investor presentation or capital-markets-day deck specific to a Slovak bank entity was located; only group-level presentations (KBC, RBI, Erste, Intesa) were found. Slovak banks are wholly owned and hold no local CMDs.

result.result_summary: Searches for SK-entity investor presentations returned press releases and annual reports instead.

why_it_matters: The 'investor presentations' element of this cell's brief resolves to parent-group decks only; expectations and collection design should be adjusted accordingly.

description: No dedicated press-release archive path was confirmed for Prima banka Slovensko, UniCredit Bank (SK site) or mBank Slovensko despite Slovak-language querying with 'tlačová správa' plus the bank name.

result.result_summary: Searches returned product pages, PDFs and third-party directory profiles instead of a newsroom listing. It is a hypothesis, not a verdict, that these banks lack one – the path may simply not be indexed.

why_it_matters: Prima banka has the densest branch footprint in Slovakia and is a plausible buyer of branch and self-service technology; missing its newsroom leaves a blind spot on that segment.

description: No press release or newsroom item was found linking any Slovak bank to a biometric onboarding / remote identity-verification vendor.

result.result_summary: The Slovak query combining bank names with 'biometrická identifikácia' and 'onboarding klient' returned only AML/identification T&Cs and generic security pages, no launch announcement naming a supplier.

why_it_matters: Biometric onboarding is an explicit topic of this cell. Either Slovak banks announce it under different wording (e.g. 'overenie totožnosti na diaľku', 'video overenie', 'selfie overenie') or these deployments are not publicly announced at all – the glossary needs extending before concluding absence.

description: KOOPERATIVA poisťovňa (VIG) produced no digitalisation or new-application press item in the Slovak-language insurer query.

result.result_summary: The combined insurer query surfaced Allianz-SP and Union material only; nothing for Kooperativa.

why_it_matters: Kooperativa is a top-three Slovak insurer; its absence is almost certainly a discovery gap rather than an absence of activity, and its newsroom must be located directly on koop.sk.

description: The routine playbook at C:/Users/User/Dropbox/E - PRINTEC GROUP/AI/MARKET RESEARCH/.../routine_prompt.md could not be read.

result.result_summary: The path is a Windows path; this agent runs on macOS and no equivalent mount was available in the working directory.

why_it_matters: Classification and scoring conventions were inferred from the task prompt alone, so they may diverge from the canonical playbook definitions.

description: No URL in this slice was fetched to confirm liveness; all entries come from search-result metadata and snippet content.

result.result_summary: URLs are reported with confidence scores only, per the hard rule that a separate deterministic pass verifies reachability.

why_it_matters: Entries with confidence below ~0.6 (Prima banka, UniCredit SK, Union poisťovňa newsroom paths) are best treated as landing-page guesses needing sitemap resolution.

description: No Diebold Nixdorf case study or customer story naming a Slovak bank surfaced in en or sk searches, despite Diebold Nixdorf s.r.o. being an active SK entity and appearing on Slovenská sporiteľňa's GDPR processor list.

result.result_summary: Relationship evidenced only indirectly (processor list, SK legal entity, PMÚ merger decision); vendor's own success-stories hub showed no SK entry in search results.

why_it_matters: Confirms the cell's structural weakness: SK wins for global ATM vendors are usually delivered through local partners and never marketed, so bank-side disclosures outrank vendor marketing for SK.

description: Auriga's customer-stories pages (EN and IT) returned no Slovak reference in search; visible examples were Portuguese and Italian banks.

result.result_summary: No SK customer story found; absence is unverified (index pages not exhaustively paged through in this pass).

why_it_matters: Suggests Auriga has not (yet) publicly displaced NCR/Printec-based ATM software in SK, but this must be re-checked directly on the index rather than inferred from search snippets.

description: Worldline/Ingenico/Nexi press searches returned only group-level M&A and non-SK market items (Germany, Austria, Belgium, Luxembourg, Ukraine); no Slovakia-specific bank acquiring or terminal partnership release was found.

result.result_summary: Group newsroom confirmed as a monitoring surface, but zero SK hits in this pass.

why_it_matters: SK acquiring relationships may be disclosed only in local-language bank/PSP communications or not at all, meaning this cell must be paired with SK-side sources.

description: Comarch, Fiserv, ACI Worldwide, Oracle Financial Services and Backbase produced no Slovakia-named customer story or case study in this pass.

result.result_summary: Only generic case-study hubs and a Fiserv SK legal entity (Bratislava) were found.

why_it_matters: For these vendors, SK presence — if any — must be inferred from local entities, job postings and procurement records rather than published references.

description: Verifone's Partner Finder appeared to list Printec Slovakia (Bratislava) per search snippet, but the locator itself is JS/interaction-driven and was not queried directly in this pass; no country-filtered SK result set was retrieved for Thales, Idemia or PAX.

result.result_summary: Locator URLs captured; SK partner lists not yet extracted.

why_it_matters: The local integrator layer is the cell's highest-value unique output; it remains only partially mapped until the locators are queried with country=Slovakia via a headless browser.

description: Most global vendors (Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos, Auriga, Temenos, Backbase, Finastra, Verifone, PAX, Thales, Idemia, Worldline) have no Slovak-language site; sk-language queries mainly returned Slovak business registers, trade media and Slovak-headquartered vendors (Asseco CE, Printec) instead.

result.result_summary: Local-language searching was performed (sk terms: referencia/referencie, banka, bankomat, tlačová správa, dodávateľ, zoznam partnerov, obchodný register) and productive — but productive on SK-side and SK-domiciled sources, not on international vendor sites.

why_it_matters: Defines the correct collection strategy: international vendor sites are monitored in English; Slovak-language effort should be spent on SK-domiciled vendors, bank disclosures, registers and trade press.

description: Gartner Peer Insights and G2 vendor comparison pages require registration and their ToS prohibit automated collection.

result.result_summary: Recorded as blocked; usable manually only under an existing licence.

why_it_matters: Review platforms cannot be part of an automated pipeline; they can serve only as occasional manual weak-signal checks.

description: No banking-sector reference material was surfaced for Slovanet a.s. in this pass; Slovanet appeared only as a client in another integrator's telecom reference list, not as a supplier to banks.

result.result_summary: Slovanet reads as a telco/connectivity provider rather than a bank software supplier; it may still supply WAN/connectivity to banks but no public evidence found.

why_it_matters: Keeping an unqualified actor in the competitor set would distort the SK supplier map; it should be demoted to a connectivity-layer supplier pending evidence.

description: Trask (CZ consultancy) could not be linked to Slovak banking delivery in this pass; queries returned Erste Group/Erste Digital material instead.

result.result_summary: No SK-specific Trask reference, office or project page found; the 'Trask/Erste' pairing in the cell definition is unverified.

why_it_matters: If Trask is not materially present in SK, the CZ-consultancy channel into SK banks runs through other firms and needs separate discovery.

description: Neither Gratex International nor DATALAN yielded a current, first-party banking reference page in search results; only third-party profiles (FinReg, RocketReach, a stale directory mirror) and an insurance-portal case study surfaced.

result.result_summary: Their live corporate domains and reference sections remain unverified; possible site restructuring or corporate reorganisation.

why_it_matters: Two of the larger named SK integrators are currently under-evidenced, leaving a hole in the prime-contractor map.

description: Ditec publishes a rich product catalogue but no client reference list naming banks; bank deployments of its e-signature stack must be inferred from other parties' materials.

result.result_summary: Product-level evidence is strong, customer-level evidence absent on the vendor's own site.

why_it_matters: Compliance-component suppliers are structurally invisible in the reference-list channel, so market share there needs a different method (tenders, conference talks, bank documentation).

description: No SK-specific Nexi presence (acquiring entity, SK-localised site, or SK terminal offer) surfaced despite a targeted bilingual query pairing Nexi with Slovak terminal/acquiring vocabulary; results returned only Worldline SK pages and generic Nexi Southern-Europe descriptions.

result.result_summary: Nexi appears in pan-European provider write-ups but no sk-SK domain, SK press release or SK licence trace was found in this pass.

why_it_matters: If Nexi has no direct SK footprint, the SK acquiring competitor set is materially narrower (Global Payments, Worldline, bank arms, domestic PSPs) and any market map that lists Nexi as an SK acquirer is wrong.

description: No Slovak terminal-hardware distributor or vendor-partner page for Ingenico, PAX or Verifone was found; the local-language query returned only US/NL resellers.

result.result_summary: SK-side hardware channel for terminal OEMs is not visible through generic search with terms 'distribútor', 'dodávateľ', 'platobné terminály'.

why_it_matters: Terminal OEM/estate share in SK is a core question for this cell; without a distributor layer it must be inferred from acquirer product pages (Worldline Yomani/Yoximo/Valina/Axium; Global Payments terminal line-up) or from public procurement and tender records.

description: Targeted search for SK merchant case studies / references published by TrustPay, Besteron, ComGate, GoPay and Barion returned comparison articles rather than any case-study or reference page.

result.result_summary: No PSP-published SK case study located via search; these usually live on vendor sites behind non-indexed paths.

why_it_matters: Case studies are the primary evidence of which merchants and verticals each PSP actually holds; they must be harvested by crawling each vendor site directly rather than via search engines.

description: TrustPay's canonical corporate domain was not returned by any search result in this pass; trustpay.eu is an inference from the entity's well-known naming and is recorded with low confidence.

result.result_summary: Entity confirmed (SK-founded 2009, NBS payment-institution licence) but URL unconfirmed.

why_it_matters: A wrong canonical domain would silently break monitoring for a top-tier domestic PSP; resolve via the NBS PSD2 register entity record before adding to collection.

description: Neither association's member list was read item-by-item in this pass. FINAS's homepage asserts 70+ members and names a handful (VISA, 365.bank, Akcenta, Prosman, SADAD, Crypto Voucher); slovakfintech.sk shows a Členstvo > členovia section but the roster itself was not enumerated here.

result.result_summary: Member-list URLs identified (finas.sk/en/membership/, slovakfintech.sk members subpage) but the full company rosters remain uncollected.

why_it_matters: The member rosters are the single highest-value artefact in this cell; a run that stops at the association homepage misses the cohort it was sent to find.

description: Slovakia has at least two bodies both rendering in English as 'Slovak FinTech Association': Slovenská FinTech asociácia (slovakfintech.sk, IČO 51910497, founded Aug 2018, exec. director Peter Papan) and FINAS – Fintech & Insurtech Association of Slovakia (finas.sk, president Davy Čajko). Third-party profiles (CB Insights, Apollo, RocketReach, LinkedIn) conflate them.

result.result_summary: Name collision confirmed across multiple sources; no evidence found of a merger or of one superseding the other.

why_it_matters: Any downstream actor map risks double-counting or attributing a member/partnership to the wrong body. Both must be tracked separately and keyed by IČO, not by name.

description: No Dealroom.co Slovakia fintech slice URL surfaced in either sk or en searching; only Tracxn, Crunchbase hubs, ensun and StartupBlink appeared. Dealroom was mentioned only second-hand as a platform that covers SK.

result.result_summary: Dealroom SK slice not located in this pass.

why_it_matters: Dealroom is a named target of this cell and is generally the strongest EU startup-funding dataset; its absence leaves a gap in funding-round coverage that Crunchbase/Tracxn only partly fill.

description: Searching in Slovak found the NBS innovation hub and regulatory sandbox pages, but no page listing which firms actually used the hub or entered the sandbox. Only the aggregate Activity Report series was found.

result.result_summary: Hub/sandbox exist and are documented; per-firm participation appears not to be published as a list.

why_it_matters: If NBS does not name participants, the earliest-entrant signal must come from the activity reports plus press coverage, not from a register — this changes the collection design.

description: Of the named EU-passported entrants, only Revolut produced concrete SK-specific evidence (sk-SK site, Revolut Bank UAB governance page, ECB licence supervised by Bank of Lithuania). No SK-specific source for Wise or Curve was located in this pass, in either language.

result.result_summary: Revolut covered; Wise and Curve uncovered.

why_it_matters: Passported entrants are competitors that never appear in SK statutory registers as licensees; if they are not tracked via their own SK-language market sites and via home-regulator passporting notifications, they are invisible to the whole programme.

description: Slovak search terms 'pasportizácia', 'zahraničné platobné inštitúcie', 'sloboda poskytovania služieb' did not surface a dedicated NBS list of inbound-passported EU payment institutions and e-money institutions serving SK cross-border.

result.result_summary: Only the general subjekty.nbs.sk register and the domestic PI/AISP listing were found.

why_it_matters: The inbound-passporting list is the definitive enumeration of EU-licensed competitors legally serving SK; without it, competitor coverage is structurally incomplete. The EBA Credit Institutions/Payment Institutions registers are the likely fallback and should be scouted next.
